examples.question_text: Isla and Finn share stickers in the ratio $5:3$. Isla receives $16$ more stickers than Finn. How many stickers does each person receive?
examples.solution_text:
The difference is $5-3=2$ parts.

$\begin{align*}2\text{ parts}&=16\text{ stickers}\\1\text{ part}&=16\div2=8\text{ stickers}\\5\text{ parts}&=5\times8=40\text{ stickers}\\3\text{ parts}&=3\times8=24\text{ stickers}\end{align*}$

Isla receives $40$ stickers and Finn receives $24$ stickers.

examples.question_text: Maya and Owen share some money in the ratio $3:5$. Maya receives $\$24$ less than Owen. How much money is shared altogether?
examples.solution_text:
The difference is $5-3=2$ parts. The total is $3+5=8$ parts.

$\begin{align*}2\text{ parts}&=\$24\\1\text{ part}&=\$24\div2=\$12\\8\text{ parts}&=8\times\$12=\$96\end{align*}$

They share $\$96$ altogether.

examples.question_text: Ava, Ben and Chloe share a prize in the ratio $2:3:7$. Chloe receives $\$36$ more than Ben. How much does Ava receive?
examples.solution_text:
Compare Chloe's $7$ parts with Ben's $3$ parts. Their difference is $7-3=4$ parts.

$\begin{align*}4\text{ parts}&=\$36\\1\text{ part}&=\$36\div4=\$9\\2\text{ parts}&=2\times\$9=\$18\end{align*}$

Ava receives $\$18$.
